button.$note: Orthogonal model — variant (treatment: filled/outline/ghost) and color (primary/secondary/destructive/success/warning/neutral) are INDEPENDENT CVA axes. Color is declared once as 4 CSS-var token refs. Only bg is read (and fg, to detect the family-less `inherit`): the tone classes are emitted per family in generate-tokens-css.js from colors.json, which is also where neutral’s on-surface/outline edge split is decided. `text` and `border` here are kept for shape and are covered by no gate, because variant-keys walks `variants` rather than `colors`. Each treatment is a fixed consumer of those vars (see shared TREATMENT_CLASSES) — no N×M compound matrix. Default filled+primary reproduces the old `default`. neutral's text/border split lets its outline stay a subtle line with readable on-surface text. INTENSITY is the third axis: color picks the family, intensity picks solid or soft. It is not a cva variant, because color and intensity together select ONE class (tone-error against tone-error-soft) and each cva axis contributes its own class independently; a lookup on the family says it without a colours-times-intensities matrix. Shared with badge through buildToneLookup, because the two drifted apart once already — badge declared containers and button declared base roles, so each could reach exactly one intensity and neither could reach the other's. NO TONE AND NO TREATMENT is spelled variant=ghost color=inherit. tone-inherit sets every --tone-* to transparent/currentColor and treat-ghost reads --tone-text, so the pair resolves to a transparent background and the inherited colour — which is what loom.base already gives a bare button, making the two restatements of each other. Reach for it when the consumer's own class owns the appearance. Note it still carries data-size, so it takes the height, padding and action font of its tier; markup written by hand as `button interactive control` takes none of those. inherit has no family and therefore no soft form, and ignores intensity.

icon-sizes.$note: Square sizing for icon-only mode (iconOnly prop). No padding — icon centers via flexbox. Touch target met at all sizes.

badge.$note: Three axes — variant (treatment: filled/outline/ghost), color (the family) and intensity (solid/soft) — matching Button exactly. The axis was called `state` until it was renamed: `state` suggests validity or interaction, and what it selects is a colour family. bg/fg name the BASE role, not the container; intensity picks the suffix, so one declaration reaches both `tone-X` and `tone-X-soft`. Declaring containers here is what made badge soft-only while Button, declaring base roles, was solid-only — each could reach exactly one intensity and neither could reach the other’s. Treatments are fixed consumers of the tone vars (shared TREATMENT_CLASSES) — no compound matrix; see buildToneLookup, which badge and button share so they cannot drift apart again. Body radius is radius/component (malleable with edges). CAUTION: the `text` and `border` keys in this colors block are read by nothing. The tone classes are emitted per family in generate-tokens-css.js from colors.json, which is also where neutral’s on-surface/outline edge split is decided; buildColorVars reads only `bg` (and `fg`, to detect the family-less `inherit`). They are kept for shape, and the variant-keys gate does not cover this block — it walks `variants`, not `colors`.

sizes.$note: Type is not declared here — it comes from the label/{tier} ramp (10/12/14), which the Figma builder has always bound to and which code now reads too. The font-size and line-height keys that used to sit on each tier were dead once code switched to the ramp, and they did not ramp anyway: sm and md both declared 10px/14px, so md differed from sm only in padding. Icons stay at 12/12/16 — against the label ramp that is 120%/100%/114% of the font and never more than 86% of the line box, where the old lg pairing put a 16px icon in 16px of leading.

sm.$exception: 2px y-padding — below spacing scale minimum (4px). Required to maintain proportional badge height at the label/sm font size.

toggle.$note: Single toggle button with pressed/unpressed states. Distinct from Switch (slider control) and Chip (selection tag). Used for toolbar actions (bold, italic), view toggles, feature on/off. aria-pressed required.

toggle-group.$note: Group of toggle buttons — exclusive (single select) or multi-select. Segmented variant: items share borders, radius collapses to first/last only (absorbs M3 segmented-button). Spaced variant: visible gaps between items, each toggle has its own borders/radius.

segmented.$note: Items touch (no gap), share borders, radius collapses to first/last only.

spaced.$note: Visible gaps between items, each toggle has its own borders/radius.
